Trap Space The single silvery-white cocoon hangs a dozen 
feet off the ground, a silken thread rises to the canopy above. 
While gently swinging in the breeze, glittering dust wafts off, 
affecting nearby creatures in a 15 ft. Emanation originating 
from the cocoon.
Countering While minuscule, the light cocoon can be seen 
when one knows to look out for it. Wisdom (Perception) Check: 
DC 10. Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
Highly sought after for its silver threads, the Moonspun 
Moth's cocoon is a rare find in the Wealdwoods. When the 
gleaming cocoon is found in the center of a clearing, many 
would-be harvesters unknowingly breath in the dust that 
gently swirl off it. Triggering wild reactions within the 
creature's hypothalamus, letting loose a piercing headache and 
uncontrollable laughter. 
Senses None
Immunities Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, 
Frightened, Prone

Moon Madness Trigger: When a creature steps within its Trap 
Space. Response - Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16, the creature 
that triggered the Trap. Failure: 5 (1d10) Psychic damage, and 
falls into a fit of hysterical laughter for 3 minutes. The target 
repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, fully aware that 
they are being affected against their will, but unable to stop the 
riotous laughter.
Trap Space The crawvine spreads a wide swath of twisting vines 
along the ground and takes up a dense 20 ft. Square of space, 
with large opened leaf lobes at the center.
Countering Easily hidden vines spread beneath the underbrush 
and leaf litter, while the wide open dark green leaf lobes, edged 
with firm gripping protrusions can be seen in the center of the 
vine mass. Wisdom (Perception) Check: DC 10. Success: The Natural 
Trap is identified.
Senses None
Immunities Blinded, Bludgeoning, Charmed, Deafened, 
Exhaustion, Frightened, Piercing, Prone
Crawvine
Gargantuan Natural Trap, Unaligned
HP 16 (3d10)
Speed 0 ft.
Reactions
Voracious Craw Trigger: When a creature steps within its Trap 
Space. Response - Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 14, the creature that 
triggered the Trap. Failure: Target creature has the Grappled 
condition (escape DC 14) and is pulled 5 ft. toward the center 
mouth of the plant every minute. Once within the center of the 
Trap Space, if the creature is Medium or smaller, it is swallowed. 
A crawvine may only swallow one creature at a time. A swallowed 
creature has the Blinded and Restrained Conditions, has Total 
Cover against attacks and other effects outside the crawvine, 
and takes 3 (1d6) Acid damage at the start of each of its turns. If 
the crawvine dies, any swallowed creatures no longer have the 
restrained condition and can escape from the plant using 5 ft. of 
movement, exiting Prone.

Trap Space While the fel floret itself is tiny, it occupies a 5 ft. 
Square and will Trigger when a creature enters that space.
Trap Space This twisting vine generally climbs 20 ft. up a tree 
and reacts to any disturbance within a 10 ft. Sphere originating 
from the tree trunk.
Countermeasures The small and unassuming fell floret is 
difficult to distinguish from nearby flora and leaf litter. Wisdom 
(Perception) Check: DC 16. Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
Countermeasures The vines twist up trees, only their distinctly 
pale green flowers reveal them. Wisdom (Perception) Check: DC 
14. Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
Fell floret flowers lay in the underbrush, hidden amongst 
fallen leaves and beneath similarly looking plants. Often found 
within dimly lit forests, the flower relies on low trophic level 
scavengers like flesh eating flies, to carry its pollen that blooms 
once a trapped corpse settles on top of it.
Twisting up tree trunks, the flowering buds of the seedspear 
vine often flourish at a dozen feet above ground level. As a 
reaction to potential predators, as well as a method for seed 
dispersal, any disturbance in the air or strong heat source, will 
pivot the flowers to launch their seeds in that direction.
Growing above spaces that have vast unseen Umbrawells cave 
complexes below the earth. The acidic earth leaves the soil 
nutrient poor and many plants, such as the crawvine have 
evolved to get their iron and phosphorus from other, more 
aggressive means.
